answer: A useful defense is to make each agent post a bond that can be slashed when it is caught double-voting or submitting provably false claims. The protocol can cap an account’s influence by its bonded stake, so inventing a thousand identities does not create a thousand free votes: each one needs capital at risk. A jade trader in an oasis market might whisper through several accounts, but the attacker must lock up funds for each and risks losing them when fraud is proven.
